title: Alsym and ERITY to develop sodium-ion energy storage systems for the mining sector
summary: Alsym Energy and ERITY have signed a 9 GWh Strategic Relationship Agreement (SRA) to jointly deploy battery energy storage systems (BESS) for the mining sector. Alsym develops sodium-ion batteries it says are non-flammable and low-cost, and ERITY is an integrated services organization that supports the mining, resources and energy sectors. Alsym’s Na-Series sodium-ion batteries are slated for deployment in existing operations and new projects run by Volt Resources and Resource Minerals International in Tanzania, Saudi Arabia, Finland and the US, as well as BESS projects for unaffiliated mining companies. ERITY operates on six continents and has major operations in Australia, Africa and the Middle East. Mining operations are often far from any grid connection, and typically run on diesel ge

title: Rethinking the high-voltage cable assembly: pre-validated and ready to install
summary: Q&A with Marc Moser, HUBER+SUHNER Ask what’s holding back electric truck and bus production and you’ll usually hear about battery supply or software. Less often mentioned: the orange highvoltage cable running between the battery, inverter, e-axle and charging port. As commercial EV volumes climb, that highvoltage power distribution has become a real constraint, and the old way of building it, one bespoke harness at a time, is straining to keep up. The argument of HUBER+SUHNER is that the fix isn’t another custom harness but a standardized, pre-validated modular cable assembly that arrives ready to install. The company calls its version mCAY, short for modular cable assembly. Launched in 2024 , the mCAY is built on the RADOX® high voltage cable line. Charged recently chatted with HUBER+SUHN

title: European Commission’s Battery Booster to invest €1.5 billion in the European battery industry
summary: The European Commission has formally established the new Battery Booster Facility, providing up to €1.5 billion from EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) revenues in the Innovation Fund to help battery cell manufacturers ramp up production in Europe. It is the first time the Commission is providing direct support in the form of interest-free loans. It has chosen loans over traditional grants “to encourage sound capital management, drive companies towards commercial viability faster and complement private sector investments.” The maximum loan per project is €500 million. “Applications will be evaluated based on their technical and financial maturity, and their added value for the European economy,” the Commission stated. The facility aims to catalyze private investment and accelerate industria

title: GM said to be working on a new EV platform
summary: The legacy automakers’ journey to electrification sometimes seems like some jerky shuffling dance—a couple of small steps forward, a step back, a pause, then another couple of steps forward. They develop an EV platform, launch some new models, then a couple of years later, they say, “EVs aren’t selling,” and cancel most of their EV programs. After a decent interval of a few months, they announce a new, super-duper EV platform. “This time we’ll get it right!” GM is currently on its third EV platform, the BEV3 architecture, which supports most of GM’s current EVs, including the Chevy Equinox and Blazer EVs and the Cadillac Lyriq , as well as the Honda Prologue and the Acura ZDX (both discontinued), and several overseas GM vehicles, including the Buick Electra E5 and E4 models in China. Now G

title: Port of Long Beach invests $58.2 million to expand vehicle and equipment electrification
summary: The Port of Long Beach has long been an early adopter of EVs and electric cargo-handling equipment. Now the port has announced an additional investment of $58.2 million to purchase and deploy more electrified equipment. The new investment will enable port tenants and operators to acquire: 61 human-operated electric cargo-handling machines along with 21 charging stations; six zero-emission harbor craft and five cleaner harbor vessels to replace older diesel-powered boats; and one zero-emission locomotive. As EVinfo.net ’s Bill Pierce notes, America’s ports represent a critical sector of our economy, but unfortunately, they are also among the most heavily polluted areas in the country. The transition to zero-emission transportation offers an opportunity to improve both public health and frei

title: The Mobility House enables smart charging and V2G for California electric school bus fleet
summary: Porterville Unified School District (PUSD), which serves communities in California’s Central Valley, is developing a comprehensive solar, battery energy storage, microgrid and EV fleet charging project, in partnership with ForeFront Power, a developer of renewable energy solutions, and The Mobility House (TMH), a charge management provider. The PUSD Zero-Emission Transportation Infrastructure Project and Microgrid will include a 763 kW solar array mounted on existing parking lot shade structures, along with a 408 kW / 1,632 kWh battery storage system. A microgrid controller will enable the facility to disconnect from Southern California Edison’s electrical grid when appropriate, drawing power directly from the district’s solar energy and battery storage assets. The system will support 35 D

title: CamMotive and Thermulon to test AEROMOTIVE thermal runaway barrier for EV batteries
summary: Electric powertrain consultancy CamMotive and aerogel developer Thermulon have been named technology partners in a £2-million, UK government-backed project to improve the safety of EV batteries. The two companies will work with an unnamed UK OEM to tackle thermal runaway in battery systems, under the government’s DRIVE35 program. The 12-month collaboration will develop and evaluate AEROMOTIVE, a UK-made aerogel-based barrier designed to contain thermal runaway in battery packs. AEROMOTIVE uses thin, lightweight layers of Anti Thermal Propagation (ATP) material to limit heat transfer between cells and slow the spread of a runaway event. Thermal runaway is one of the central safety challenges in lithium-ion batteries. Under certain fault conditions a cell can heat uncontrollably, triggering

title: Radius gives its customers access to Milence’s European heavy-duty electric truck charging network
summary: Business mobility provider Radius has added the Milence charging network to its list of partners. The Milence charging network is built specifically to serve heavy goods vehicles (HGVs) in long-haul operations. It features high-power charging stations, including MCS chargers , strategically located along key logistics corridors in Europe. Milence launched its first charging hub in the Netherlands in 2023, and now has 38 hubs operational across Europe. Through access to the Milence network, Radius customers can now benefit from charging infrastructure designed specifically for trucks, including hubs with the space, accessibility and power required for heavy-duty, long-haul operations. Radius customers can locate nearby charging stations through the Radius e-route app. “The transition to ele

title: Flux Power’s SkyEMS 3.0 adds battery-health analytics and customizable dashboards
summary: Flux Power has released SkyEMS 3.0 , the latest version of its fleet energy-management platform for lithium-ion battery packs. The update centers on customizable dashboards, AI-driven analytics and battery-health monitoring, all of which is designed to give operators a configurable view of how their batteries are charging, working and aging. Flux Power’s packs run mainly in material handling equipment such as forklifts and in airport ground support equipment (GSE), applications in which unplanned battery downtime stalls operations. The dashboard is the core of the redesign. Drag-and-drop widgets let each user choose the metrics that matter to them: state of charge, charging activity, fleet utilization, runtime performance and battery health trends. Teams can configure alerts around specifi

title: Integrals Power to supply LMFP cathode material to EU-funded OLiMPUS battery project
summary: UK battery materials company Integrals Power will supply its lithium manganese iron phosphate (LMFP) cathode active material to OLiMPUS, a €9-million Horizon Europe project that aims to develop LMFP battery cells using a European supply chain. The company will provide more than 150 kg of the manganese-rich material, and is also responsible for scaling up and industrializing the manufacturing process and supporting cell prototyping and validation. OLiMPUS brings together 16 partners from across the battery value chain, including Volvo Trucks, Magna Steyr, cell manufacturer Verkor, synthetic graphite anode supplier Vianode and maritime energy storage specialist Corvus Energy. The project will run until 2030 and will produce more than 130 automotive-grade cells on SINTEF’s pilot lines and at

title: Alpine provides preview of the electric A110
summary: Renault's sports car brand Alpine unveiled the prototype of the future electric A110 in motion to the public for the first time at the Goodwood Festival of Speed. The electric sports car is based on the new Alpine Performance Platform with 800 volts.

title: BMW falls below previous year’s battery-electric vehicle sales
summary: BMW has released its delivery figures for the first half of the year—and the parallels with other German automakers are obvious: BMW, too, is weakened by the crumbling China business. And like its German peers, BMW is currently finding the most stability for its EV sales in Europe.

title: Gone to the dogs: Peugeot unveils E-5008 Dog Edition
summary: Peugeot has unveiled the E-5008 Dog Edition Concept, a concept study aimed at dog owners. The one-off combines special equipment features and software functions for traveling with four-legged companions but is not yet planned for series production.

title: Volkswagen Group loses ground in battery-electric vehicle sales
summary: The Volkswagen Group reports 438,500 all-electric vehicle deliveries for its brands in the first half of the year. This represents a 5.8 per cent decrease compared to the same period last year. BEV sales have declined significantly, particularly in the USA and China. However, in the important European market, Volkswagen recorded a rate of eight per cent growth.

title: Mercedes-AMG unveils electric CLA 45 with three axial-flux motors
summary: Mercedes-AMG is expanding the electric CLA line-up with a particularly high-performance variant. The new CLA 45 4MATIC+ features three axial flux motors, a system output of 500 kW, and is set to be offered in two body versions.

title: Eviny and Mer merge to become Northern Europe’s largest fast-charging provider
summary: Norwegian charging infrastructure companies Eviny Fast Charging and the Statkraft subsidiary Mer are merging. According to their own statements, the joint company will become the largest fast-charging provider in Nordic countries and is expected to also integrate Mer's public charging business in Germany in the future.

title: LG Energy Solution likely to increase battery supply for Tesla
summary: LG Energy Solution is apparently expanding the production of cylindrical battery cells at the South Korean company's plant in Nanjing, China. According to a South Korean media report, the expanded capacities are intended to cover Tesla's growing orders.

title: Grab plans fifteenfold expansion of its charging network in Vietnam
summary: Drivers of electric cars and motorcycles in Vietnam will soon benefit from the fifteenfold expansion of Southeast Asian ride-hailing and delivery giant Grab's electric-vehicle charging network, from about 400 ports at present to more than 6,000 by 2028. Nearly half of the planned charging ports will be located in the capital, Hanoi.

title: SINEXCEL launches one-stop solution for e-truck charging
summary: SINEXCEL has unveiled a solar-storage-charging solution for Europe's heavy-duty electric truck market, themed ‘From Watts to Ton-Kilometers, Empower Euro€ with Every Watt’. Focusing on power-transport integration, the solution combines charging, energy storage and software to address grid constraints and improve fleet economics.

title: China exports over half a million plug-in cars for first time in June
summary: The Chinese market for New Energy Vehicles (NEV) reached a new record in June. Almost six out of ten newly sold vehicles had an alternative drive system. At the same time, auto exports exceeded the half-million mark for NEVs in a single month for the first time.

title: First drive in the new Audi Q4 e-tron: does the facelift measure up?
summary: The Q4 e-tron has been Audi's electric bestseller since 2021, with over 400,000 units sold to date. However, the technology had become outdated. With the 2026 facelift, Audi is making significant upgrades, particularly in the interior, and introducing two genuine innovations. During a first test drive at Lake Tegernsee, it becomes clear where the updated Q4 excels – and which question remains unanswered.

title: India: Delhi adds 300 electric buses to its public transport fleet
summary: Indian capital Delhi on Tuesday deployed 300 electric buses for public transport use. Delhi government also inaugurated four electric bus depots on the same day.

title: Ford issues US recall of Mustang Mach-E electric crossovers
summary: The recall affects certain Mach-Es from the 2021, 2022, and 2023 model years, due to a potential issue with the rear differential. According to the NHTSA, the vehicles in question have a rear differential pinion shaft at risk of fracture.

title: Kia EV2 Long Range now eligible for UK Electric Car Grant
summary: Kia UK has confirmed that the EV2 Long Range is now eligible for the maximum Band 1 Electric Car Grant. It reduces the vehicle's on-the-road price by £3,750.

title: Allego switches operator backend to Ampeco
summary: Dutch charging provider Allego is switching to Ampeco for the backend of its charging network. The new charge point management software will be used to manage over 35,000 charging points across 16 European countries. The migration is expected to be completed in Q4 2026.

title: China targets 30 per cent NEV fleet by 2030
summary: China has published its action plan to limit the peak of CO₂ emissions. By 2030, vehicles with alternative powertrains are to account for 30 per cent of the nation's total vehicle fleet. At the same time, the government wants to accelerate the expansion of charging and hydrogen infrastructure.

title: Posco and Hyundai develop novel electrical steel for more efficient electric motors
summary: Posco is launching a project with Hyundai Motor and other partners to develop high-silicon electrical steel - a precursor material for stator and rotor production. The goal is to increase the efficiency of electric motors and advance the material technology to series application in EVs.

title: Fiat Topolino now available in US – but it’s not road-legal
summary: Just days after opening UK order books for the Topolino, it appears Fiat is continuing its westward expansion: the diminutive electric quadricycle is now available to order in the USA. However, it's yet to be made road-legal.

title: FirstGroup brand to operate ZEV shuttle service at Sizewell C
summary: Specialist Passenger Solutions (SPS) has landed a contract to operate shuttle services to and from the Sizewell C nuclear plant construction site in Suffolk. It plans to operate a 'zero emission' fleet comprised of both hydrogen and electric buses.

title: A steep learning curve: how Spedition Stickel is building its battery-electric truck ecosystem
summary: The German logistics company Stickel is putting more of its freight on electric trucks, with a fleet of ten now in operation. We spoke with managing director Christian Stickel about investment willingness, initial complexity, and the confidence needed to embrace a new energy future.

title: VW Board reportedly aims for plant closures starting in 2031
summary: Led by Group CEO Oliver Blume, VW's executive board reportedly plans to phase out production at its Zwickau and Emden plants by 2031 with the Hanover factory set to follow in 2032, and the Neckarsulm Audi plant in 2034. This information was obtained by the German magazine Der Spiegel ahead of the VW Supervisory Board meeting this afternoon.

title: AESC launches mass production of new 46120 cylindrical cells for the BMW iX5
summary: AESC has started series production of its new 46120 round cells. The battery cells are set to supply several BMW Group EVs in the future. The first announced model to feature the new cells is the all-electric BMW iX5, whose market launch is planned for late 2026 or early 2027.

title: University of Kiel develops battery sensor-based communication system
summary: Researchers at Kiel University have developed a new communication system for battery cells. The method enables sensor data from inside a battery to be transmitted without additional data lines - potentially making battery management systems simpler, more cost-effective, and safer.

title: Asleep at the wheel: Tesla video sparks debate
summary: A video from Canada appears to show a driver asleep behind the wheel of a Tesla - while in motion. The incident raises renewed questions about the use of driver assistance systems like Tesla's 'Full Self Driving'.

title: Industry calls on EU to simplify state aid for cleantech factories
summary: A coalition of industrial companies, investors, and associations is urging the EU Commission to revise its rules regarding state aid and cleantech production. In an open letter, the signatories advocate for predictable production subsidies to enable investments in battery factories and other climate-friendly technologies in Europe.

title: Renault refreshes Master E-Tech with battery and comfort upgrades
summary: Renault has updated the Master E-Tech Electric. The electric van now features a chemically redesigned 87kWh battery, new comfort and safety functions, as well as a range of additional variants for different applications. A new chassis-cab version with a 40kWh battery is also available for urban use.

title: Leapmotor launches first electric van in China
summary: Leapmotor is launching its first van in China. The seven-seater D99 will be available as a pure electric model and as a range-extender vehicle, starting at a price equivalent to just over €32,000. It is not yet known whether the D99 will be offered outside China in future.

title: Wren Kitchens begins electrification of heavy goods fleet
summary: The UK kitchen retailer Wren Kitchens has begun its fleet electrification journey, following the delivery of 10 electric Mercedes-Benz eActros 600 tractor units. It marks the start of the company's broader ambitions to operate an all-electric HGV fleet.

title: Nio builds battery research centre in Shanghai
summary: Nio plans to construct a new research and development center for battery technologies in Shanghai in the second half of the year. The facility will focus on next-generation batteries and will include a pilot line for lithium-ion cells as well as 31 test laboratories.

title: OMV Petrom completes network of 384 fast-charging points
summary: Romanian energy company OMV Petrom has installed 384 fast-charging points at 92 locations in Slovakia, Hungary, and Romania as part of an EU-funded major project. Approximately a quarter of the investment volume was covered by the EU.

title: Mercedes AMG CLA 45 arrives in Goodwood with 680 hp and three axial-flux motors
summary: Merceds took the wraps off its new Mercedes-AMG CLA 45 4MATIC+ at this weekend’s Goodwood Festival of Speed, with jaw-dropping specs, staggering acceleration, and rising Formula 1 star Kimi Antonelli behind the wheel.

title: Volvo Electric semi trucks charge up American Truck Simulator
summary: American Truck Simulator’s players can finally get a taste of what it’s like to climb into the cab of a Volvo VNL and VNR Electric semi trucks as the big BEVs become the first-ever electric truck to be featured in the over-the-road driving game.

title: VMAX launches new full-suspension VX2 Lite e-scooter for a mere $799
summary: Swiss electric scooter maker VMAX has launched the new VX2 Lite , a commuter-focused electric scooter that packs premium features like full suspension, a 56-mile (90 km) maximum range, and up to 1,400W of peak motor power into a relatively lightweight package.

title: Tesla claims Cybercab driving employees at Giga Texas — in a parking lot
summary: Tesla says “Cybercab employee rides at Giga Texas” are “starting soon” — its first stated step toward putting people inside the wheel-less, pedal-less robotaxi. But the announcement, spread across two Tesla accounts and roughly 2.9 million combined views, is thinner than it sounds. It’s not clear whether Tesla means Cybercabs running a real ride service in Austin or simply driving employees around a factory parking lot.

title: Another state adds a way to report reckless e-bike and e-scooter riders
summary: As communities across the US continue grappling with the rapid rise of electric bikes and scooters, one Oregon sheriff’s office is introducing a new tool designed to help identify trouble spots before someone gets hurt.

title: UNIGRID’s sodium-ion home battery debuts in Europe, US is next
summary: Lithium-ion has long dominated home battery storage, but sodium-ion is starting to make its move. Sodium-ion battery startup UNIGRID has shipped the first units of its Na+Casa residential battery, with the first systems now installed in homes across Europe.

title: Musk tells Tesla staff to switch to Grok — a model he admits is worse
summary: Elon Musk told Tesla staff to move to using Grok, the AI model from his own xAI (now folded into SpaceX), according to a memo sent to employees on Friday. The push comes days after Tesla capped employee spending on third-party AI tools — and it lands even though Musk himself concedes Grok is not as good as its rivals.

title: BYD’s $10,000 Seagull EV revealed with a longer body and more upgrades
summary: BYD’s low-cost Seagull EV, sold as the Dolphin Surf in Europe, is getting another update with a longer body and a more powerful motor.

title: Podcast: Rivian goes to market, Xiaomi goes big, and a $14,000 tiny EV in the US
summary: In the Electrek Podcast , we discuss the most popular news in the world of sustainable transport and energy. In this week’s episode, we discuss Rivian going back to the stock market market, Xiaomi going big, and a $14,000 tiny EV in the US.

title: These are the top 10 best-selling EVs in the US so far in 2026
summary: Tesla is still the king, accounting for about 50% of the US EV market, but a handful of brands are finally gaining traction with new models now on sale.

title: Xiaomi reveals SkyNomad N90: a living room on wheels
summary: Xiaomi has revealed the SkyNomad N90, the first model in its new SkyNomad series and the company’s first extended-range electric vehicle. CEO Lei Jun posted the first official exterior images today, and a new regulatory filing confirmed the full specs. The N90 is a full-size, three-row SUV with a claimed combined range of more than 1,500 km (932 miles), aimed squarely at Li Auto and Huawei-backed Aito in China’s fast-growing EREV market.

summary: Closing out this week’s Green Deals is the newly launched Lectric 250th Anniversary Sale with up to $464 increased savings from its July 4th deals on three e-bikes – the XP4 750, Xpress2, and Xpeak2 – all starting from $1,299 . title: Volkswagen’s EV van makes a surprise comeback in the US as the ID.4 goes on hiatus
summary: Ahead of the updated 2027 model, sales of Volkswagen’s electric minibus bounced back, rising 120%. Meanwhile, the ID.4 is on a brief hiatus as it undergoes a major refresh.

title: Toyota is promising big things for the Lexus LFA EV sports car, but will we ever get to see it?
summary: Toyota’s luxury marque is bringing back its iconic sports car as an EV. The all-electric Lexus LFA made a public appearance at the Goodwood FOS, but will it ever reach production?

title: Australia’s 7 best-selling EVs are now all Chinese — even Tesla’s
summary: Australia just posted its biggest month ever for electric car sales, and for the first time seven different EVs each cleared 1,000 units in a single month. Every one of them is either Chinese-owned or Chinese-built — and that includes the Tesla Model Y that topped the chart, which rolls off the line in Shanghai.

title: BYD wins 11.3 GWh battery deal for world’s largest solar+storage
summary: BYD Energy Storage has landed a contract to supply 11.275 GWh of battery storage for Masdar’s Round the Clock (RTC) project in Abu Dhabi — one of the single largest energy storage procurements ever signed. The RTC project pairs a 5.2 GW solar array with a 19 GWh battery system, making it the world’s largest combined solar-plus-storage plant. BYD’s award covers the majority of that storage.

title: Yamaha launches sporty Aerox-E electric scooter with removable batteries
summary: Yamaha has officially entered India’s increasingly competitive premium electric scooter market with the launch of the new Aerox-E , an electric version of its popular sporty maxi-scooter. Rather than chasing outright affordability, Yamaha is targeting riders looking for performance-focused urban transportation with premium features. That has resulted in a more premium scooter, but also one of the highest scooter price tags in the country.

title: Global EV sales hit 2 million in June – and the US falls further behind
summary: Global EV sales topped 2 million in June, but the headline numbers hide a widening split between the world’s biggest markets.

title: Hyundai launches affordable EV deals with 0% APR and up to $10,000 off
summary: Hyundai’s biggest sales promo of the year, the Getaway Summer Sales Event, kicked off this month with competitive offers on its most popular vehicles, including EVs.

title: SolarEdge says its new ‘Lego-like’ home battery installs in under 30 minutes
summary: SolarEdge is rolling out its next-generation home solar and battery storage platform across the US, with orders for SolarEdge Nexis now open.

title: China’s giant Gobi solar plant runs after dark on salt, not batteries
summary: China Three Gorges Corporation (CTG) has put the world’s largest solar PV-plus-concentrated-solar hybrid into commercial trial operation in the Gobi Desert — and its headline trick is delivering power after sunset without a single lithium battery. The 1-gigawatt Hami project in Xinjiang stores the sun’s energy as heat in molten salt, letting it keep generating for up to eight hours after dark.

title: Trump clean energy rollbacks erase $68B in US investment
summary: The Trump administration’s rollback of clean energy policies has now cost the US nearly 470,000 jobs and $68 billion in private investment, according to a new report released today.

title: BYD launches the Dolphin G plug-in hatch with 65 miles of EV range for $32,000
summary: The Dolphin G DM-i is BYD’s first car specifically designed for Europe. With up to 65 miles of pure electric range and 646 miles combined, BYD said the plug-in hatch will redefine the segment as an affordable, efficient alternative. It’s now available to order, starting at about $32,000.

title: Toyota delays Highlander BEV production as the 3-row electric SUV is put on the back burner
summary: Toyota is delaying production of its first three-row electric SUV, the 2027 Highlander BEV, as it extends the current gas and hybrid models.

summary: We’ve stuffed today’s Green Deals with plenty of summer savings, starting with EcoFlow’s Outdoor Season Sale and up to 57% power station discounts from $259, like the 3,072Wh DELTA 3 Ultra Portable Power Station down at $1,299 . As part of Velotric’s World Cup Sale deals , you can find the Discover 2 Step-Thru Comfort Commuter e-bike with Apple Find My, SensorSwap tech, and a 75-mile range down at its second-lowest $1,799 pricing. title: MG is launching its first PHEV with semi-solid-state batteries in 2027
summary: MG’s semi-solid-state batteries will not be exclusive to EVs, with plans to launch three new plug-in hybrid SUVs equipped with the new battery tech. First up will be the MG ZS PHEV, set to go on sale in 2027.

title: New bill would ban Tesla’s camera-only Robotaxi, not Waymo
summary: New Jersey lawmakers are advancing a bill that would require driverless commercial vehicles to carry cameras plus two additional sensor types — a mandate Tesla’s camera-only Robotaxi can’t meet. The proposed law, S1677, would effectively lock Tesla out of the most densely populated US state unless it adds the radar and lidar hardware that Elon Musk has spent years insisting his cars don’t need.

title: BYD reveals prices for its new 1,500hp+ luxury EV sports car start at nearly $200K [Images]
summary: BYD took the covers off its new drop-top electric sports car at the Goodwood FOS. The Denza Z packs over 1,500 hp and can recharge in as little as 5 minutes, but it’s not cheap.

title: Trek targets the fat tire e-bike boom with its new throttle-enabled Borrego+
summary: Trek is making a bigger push into the fast-growing fat tire e-bike segment with the launch of the new Borrego+, a Class 2 electric bike that blends adventure-ready capability with commuter-friendly practicality. The company is also offering a faster Borrego+ S variant for riders in markets where Class 3 e-bikes are permitted.

title: Xiaomi says Sky Nomad is a series, not a new brand, teases SUV
summary: Xiaomi has answered the biggest open question about Sky Nomad: it’s a second product series under Xiaomi EV, not the standalone sub-brand that had been rumored for months. The company also revealed the first clear look at the lineup’s debut model — a rugged, boxy extended-range SUV — in a set of official teaser posters.

title: Volkswagen put 100 sheep to work under 31,000 solar panels
summary: Volkswagen has traded lawnmowers for sheep at the massive solar farm that helps power one of its factories in Poland, and the animals are doing more than just keeping the grass short.

title: Kia’s electric hatch gains AWD and nearly 350 miles of range
summary: Kia launched the new all-wheel drive (AWD) EV4 variant in Europe, but it’s not quite the range-topping GT model.

title: What I saw inside Lectron’s EV charger factory in China
summary: Whether you know the Lectron name or not, there’s a good chance you’ve used one of its EV charging adapters. The company makes many of the J1772/CCS-to-NACS and NACS-to-J1772/CCS adapters that EV drivers rely on. Now, Lectron has launched the NEXUS, its second-gen Level 2 home EV charger. I recently toured Lectron’s factory in China to see how the company has become a go-to supplier for both EV drivers and automakers like Ford, GM, and Mercedes-Benz.

title: Sunrun wants to pay you to turn your home into an AI data center
summary: Sunrun wants to turn thousands of solar-powered homes into a giant distributed AI data center – and pay homeowners to help power the AI boom.

title: Ford admits its $30K midsize EV pickup is actually ‘small’
summary: Ford’s midsize EV pickup, due out next year, will be smaller than expected. For the first time, Ford referred to it as an “all-new, affordable small electric pickup” built on the UEV platform.

title: China is bringing buttons back to cars, ending trend led by Tesla
summary: China will require automakers to include physical buttons for safety-related functions, pushing back on the proliferation of using screens for everything in modern cars.

title: Lectric XP4 750 e-bike gets FREE $498 flash sale cargo bundle, Navee Summer EV Sale, EGO Select Cut + Touch Drive mower $599, more
summary: At the front of our midweek Green Deals pack is a cargo-focused flash sale on Lectric’s XP4 750 Folding Utility e-bike with a $498 FREE bundle at $1,299 . Coming up behind it is Navee’s Summer Sale lineup of EV deals, like the UT5 Max Electric SuperScooter at its $1,300 low , as well as EGO’s advanced 21-inch Cordless Electric Select Cut + Touch Drive Lawn Mower kit at a $599 2026 low , the meross Wi-Fi 2-Zone Water Timer for Garden Hoses at $88 , a returning low price on Govee’s Matter Outdoor Lamp Post – plus, some solid camping-ready deals and soon-to-end holiday sales. As always, you can also find the latest hangover deals down at the bottom of the page, like yesterday’s Anker SOLIX Summer Power Sale exclusive power station deals, the returning $299 low on ECOVACS’ Ultramarine P1 cordl

title: Xiaomi makes Sky Nomad official: new EREV brand to take on Li Auto
summary: Xiaomi officially confirmed “Sky Nomad,” the name of its new extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) effort, after months of rumors. The first model is a full-size SUV expected to deliver over 1,500 km (932 miles) of combined range. The announcement puts China’s hottest EV newcomer on a collision course with Li Auto and Huawei-backed Aito, which dominate the country’s lucrative family SUV segment.

title: This $22K EV coupe has a semi-solid-state battery and a ‘Queen’ makeup station in China

summary: Chinese automaker Chery has started assembling its retro-style electric SUV, the V23, in Thailand, deepening its roots in the country. Thailand is the second country in the ASEAN region after Indonesia where the company offers a locally assembled V23.

summary: Michelin’s Connected Solutions Division (CXS) has added 19 new EVs to its UK fleet. summary: Vietnamese automaker VinFast has introduced the VF 2 electric city car and launched it first in its home market. The VF 2 is simply a premium version of the Minio Green, part of the company's Green range of commercial and service mobility vehicles.

summary: According to certification applications, the Volkswagen Group is preparing to launch three new electric models in China. The battery-powered sedans ID. UNYX 09 and Jetta M6, as well as the electric SUV ID.Aura T6, are expected to hit the market this year. Two of the three EVs were developed in collaboration with Xpeng.

summary: The University of Nottingham and GKN Aerospace have established HPDrive Technologies to develop cryogenic electrical machine technologies. The new company will focus on applications in hydrogen-electric aviation and other high-power sectors.

summary: The UK government will introduce its new mileage-based Electric Vehicle Excise Duty (eVED) from April 2028. Following a consultation with more than 5,000 respondents, ministers have simplified compliance requirements for fleets and dropped additional mileage checks for newer vehicles.

summary: Bosch has signed a funding agreement with the US Department of Commerce worth up to $225 million. The funds will go toward expanding semiconductor manufacturing in Roseville, California, where silicon carbide chips will be produced—primarily for electric vehicles.

title: Falcon Buses rolls out first electric buses – and depot upgrades
summary: Falcon Buses, a small Surrey-based bus operator, is set to deploy a fleet of 13 new electric buses on routes across the county. The public transport company has also installed charging infrastructure at its Byfleet depot.

summary: Construction of the Fraunhofer Research Manufacturing Battery Cell facility in Münster has reached another milestone, with the project celebrating its midway point this week. title: California launches instant EV rebates for first-time buyers
summary: California will introduce a new point-of-sale rebate programme for first-time zero-emission vehicle buyers later this summer. Backed by $135.5 million in state funding and matching contributions from automakers, the initiative forms part of a broader $600 million clean transport package. The initiative, branded MyFirstEV, will launch later this summer.

title: Ford Pro delivers 131 electric vans to BVG

The charging stations will be designed specifically for heavy-duty electric vehicles. Each site will feature between 3 and 36 charging points, and a total power rating of up to 1 MW. summary: Southwest Research Institute (SwRI) and Southern Methodist University (SMU) are collaborating on a design architecture for solid-state batteries. That combination, according to SwRI, enables faster charging and higher energy density, and replacing flammable liquids with solid materials makes operation inherently safer. In SwRI’s design, as solid lithium metal anode sits in direct contact with the solid electrolyte. title: MOIA launches autonomous ride-pooling service in Hamburg

summary: Michelin has added 19 Ford electric vans to its UK Connected Solutions Division fleet, taking the share of battery-electric vehicles to almost two-thirds. The deployment includes three E-Transit Custom vans and 16 E-Transit Courier models, which replace diesel-powered vehicles.

summary: Electric mobility continues to expand across the Nordic countries. Norway remains the clear leader with the highest share of electric cars, while Denmark is rapidly catching up in terms of growth. OFV’s half-year report shows that the electrification of passenger car fleets is continuing to advance.

title: Clean Motion trials battery swapping for solar delivery vans
summary: Swedish manufacturer Clean Motion has equipped its lightweight electric vehicle EVIG with a swappable battery and launched real-world trials in Stockholm. The vehicle uses GoCimo’s existing battery-swapping infrastructure and is being tested in urban operations, including Foodora’s delivery service.

title: ID. Cross to become Volkswagen’s electric SUV entry model
summary: With the VW ID. Cross, the last of the four new all-electric compact cars from the Volkswagen Group is celebrating its world premiere: The new model aims to appeal to those looking for an unpretentious, spacious city car with SUV styling. For VW, the ID. Cross, alongside the ID. Polo, is the most important product launch of the year.

summary: The Port of Los Angeles has opened a $75 million funding programme to support the deployment of battery-electric Class 8 drayage trucks. Eligible operators can receive up to $300,000 per vehicle as the port seeks to accelerate the transition to zero-emission freight transport.

summary: Generational has signed a distribution agreement with Maverick Diagnostics to bring EV battery health testing to around 6,000 workshops across the UK. title: Cupra launches cheaper Raval from €30,000
summary: Cupra is introducing a more affordable variant of its electric compact car, the Raval. The Raval Plus, featuring a 99-kW electric motor and a 37-kWh battery, starts at €29,850 and can now be configured in Germany. title: High-potential testing for EVs: why reed relays raise confidence in insulation and safety

That is the role of high-potential testing. In a withstand test the product is stressed above normal operating voltage and leakage is measured. In a breakdown test the voltage is increased until insulation fails so that safe design margins can be set. Both require precise control of kilovolt sources, very low leakage measurement and safe discharge paths. Scientists at the US Department of Energy’s Argonne National Laboratory combined computation and experiment to identify protective coatings for sulfide-based solid electrolytes, and pointed to magnesium oxide in particular. Solid-state batteries could store more energy and improve safety compared with today’s lithium-ion cells, but some solid electrolytes are chemically fragile. Applications include electronics, automotive parts, batteries and consumer goods. The new system, called Mars, runs at speeds up to 2.5 feet per second and comes in both 2D and 2.5D arrayed configurations. High-voltage systems in electrified vehicle and renewable applications can run into the thousands of volts, so test setups often add external dividers to scale the signal down before it reaches the analyzer. title: Rivian R2 uses up to 26% more energy than Model Y in real-world test
summary: Out of Spec Reviews put a Rivian R2 Performance and a Tesla Model Y Performance on the same roads on the same afternoon. The R2 used 18% to 26% more energy at every single speed they tested. That’s awkward, because the two SUVs carry identical EPA efficiency ratings, and Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe has been telling media the R2 matches the Model Y.

title: BMW Is Finally Planning An Electric Convertible: Report
summary: The BMW i4 Convertible will come with two doors, four seats, and a power folding soft-top, according to a new report.

title: Things Are Getting Really, Really Bad At Porsche. That's Not Good For EV Fans
summary: The company is cutting 20% of its jobs by 2035. Some key models could be axed, too.

title: The Rivian R2 Is A Charging Beast. But It's 'Just Fine' At Road Tripping
summary: Rivian stuck with 400-volt battery architecture for the R2 to save costs but that hasn't weakened its ability to charge quickly at all.

title: Inside BMW's Plan To Produce The iX5’s Gigantic Battery Pack In The U.S.
summary: While several automakers step back from EVs, BMW is staying on course with new models and local battery production.

title: New report: DC-coupled energy hubs reduce costs and overcome grid constraints for EV fleets
summary: Microgrids are a hot topic these days, and with good reason—supporting EV charging infrastructure with battery storage, on-site generation and V2X technology can overcome grid constraints and reduce costs. Cenex has published new research detailing how DC-coupled smart energy hubs can help organisations accelerate fleet electrification while unlock substantial energy savings, lower peak demand and overcome grid constraints. The report explores the performance of the 3ti Papilio3 V2X DC FastHub across a range of commercial and public-sector use cases, including fleet depots, factories, offices and leisure destinations. Using Cenex’s EIGER energy modelling tool, the study assessed how DC-coupled energy systems can optimise energy use behind the meter. The report found that peak site demand c

title: TDK’s EP21 common-mode chokes handle up to 35 A in an SMD package
summary: TDK has introduced the EP21 series of flat-wire double chokes (ordering code B82552J*J021). The company intends them for common-mode filtering in DC-DC converters and other low-voltage EMC protection circuits. The parts share a 23.8 x 17.7 mm footprint and stand 21.6 to 22.3 mm tall, depending on the version. The terminations sit under the body of the component, which TDK says minimizes the board space it occupies. The four-pin layout improves mechanical reliability, according to the company. Rated voltage is 48 V AC or 80 V DC. Rated currents run from 20.3 to 35 A and need no derating up to 70° C. Above that temperature the parts must be derated. Four versions make up the series, and inductance trades off against current rating across them. The 160 µH version carries 35 A at a DC resistan

title: Connecticut selects AmpUp to scale Adapt & Earn managed EV charging program
summary: The Connecticut Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (PURA) has selected AmpUp to develop a managed EV charging program in collaboration with the state’s electric utilities. The agency evaluated four pilots in Cycle 1 of the state’s Innovative Energy Solutions (IES) Program, and selected AmpUp’s Adapt & Earn managed charging project for deployment at scale. PURA has invited AmpUp and Connecticut’s electric utilities to jointly propose a statewide program design, creating a pathway to expand managed charging at public and shared EV chargers across the state. Managed charging saves energy and improves grid flexibility by allowing utilities to limit EV charging power at times of peak demand. Utilities have done this with air conditioners and other power-hungry loads for decades, and setting

title: EVSearch reports surging Canadian demand for Chinese EVs
summary: Chinese EVs are headed for Canada. The country has set an initial annual quota of 49,000 Chinese-made EVs, and this will increase to 70,000 within five years. A share of the quota is reserved for vehicles priced below CA$35,000. EVSearch , a Canadian electric vehicle research and discovery platform, has added a new section to its site dedicated to Chinese EVs. Since its quiet beta launch, the Chinese EV Discovery Center has logged over 25,000 users and 130,000 page views, making it the platform’s fastest-growing research category. EVSearch’s information hub includes a virtual showroom of EV and PHEV models available in Canada, an EV Charging Cost Calculator and a Battery Health Estimator for pre-owned EVs. The Chinese EV Discovery Center provides vehicle specifications, estimated Canadian

title: Wevo’s WEVOSIL silicone gap filler can fill millimeter-scale battery pack gaps
summary: German potting and adhesives manufacturer Wevo-Chemie has introduced a new thermally conductive silicone gap filler for compact assemblies such as high-voltage battery packs and power electronics. Wevo’s WEVOSIL 26040 FL gap filler is rated at 4 W/m·K and can be applied at bondlines of less than 70 µm. The material has a thermal conductivity of 3 W/m·K and a density of 2.22 g/cm³. Wevo says conventional paste-like gap fillers with high viscosity quickly reach their limits when gaps measure only a few millimeters, and that the new material can be applied reliably in tight spaces. It can be laid down as a bead and compressed into place under low pressure. If no free areas need to be connected, it can also be injected into the gap, and Wevo says its high sag resistance keeps it from flowing b

title: Download trend paper: Supercharging data connectivity to meet next-generation automotive expectations
summary: Sponsored by TTI & TE Connectivity. Automotive consumers demand more personalization, autonomy and connectivity from their driving experience. To make this a reality, connectivity plays a pivotal role in vehicle innovation design requirements. The next generation of vehicles needs more cameras to support advanced driver-assistance system (ADAS) and autonomous driving (AD) functionalities.​ The cameras need to be smaller in size while also providing a higher resolution for more detailed views for the driver. For these newer compact yet powerful cameras, the connectors used will be required to support higher bit rates while also offering a new level of physical integration into the device itself. Download this trend paper to learn about the future of vehicle technology and the connectivity s

title: Freenow and Apollo Go launch London robotaxi trial
summary: Freenow by Lyft and Baidu's autonomous driving unit Apollo Go have launched road tests of robotaxis in London. The trials mark the first concrete step in implementing the commercial robotaxi partnership the two companies announced for Europe in 2025.

title: Hongqi unveils 12C ultra-fast charging battery
summary: Hongqi says its new battery charged from 10 to 70 per cent in under four minutes during tests. The development marks another step in China's race to cut EV charging times with ultra-fast battery technology.

title: Pilot brings smart charging to Gelderland’s public charge points
summary: A pilot project involving 12,000 public charging points is launching in the Dutch province of Gelderland to reward EV drivers for charging at grid-friendly times. The six project partners aim to assess whether financial incentives for flexible charging behaviour can help reduce peak loads on the electricity grid.

title: Hyundai recalls Inster over fire risk
summary: Just months after the Hyundai Inster established itself in the market, the Korean carmaker has launched a major safety recall. Due to a potential fire risk, Hyundai is recalling around 40,000 units of its battery-electric compact car worldwide, including approximately 14,610 vehicles in Germany.

title: BYD commences sales of Racco electric kei car in Japan
summary: In a major step toward making deeper inroads into the Japanese auto market, BYD has commenced sales of its electric kei car, the Racco. The company manufactures this model in Changzhou (Jiangsu Province), China, and says it is the first kei car designed by any overseas automaker.

title: ACEA reports strong growth for electric trucks and buses in the EU
summary: The EU commercial vehicle market grew in the first half of 2026, with electric trucks and buses continuing to gain ground. Battery-electric truck registrations rose by 47.7%, while electric buses captured 27.7% of the market, although ACEA says uptake remains too slow overall.

title: Bosch trials fuel cell bus technology in Madrid
summary: Bosch has started real-world testing of its new fuel cell system for buses in Madrid. The company is trialling the technology in an Irizar bus operating on the Spanish capital's public transport network.

title: BMW reportedly plans electric i4 Cabrio for 2028
summary: Following the impending end of the BMW i4 Gran Coupé, the Munich-based automaker apparently plans to introduce a fully electric i4 Cabriolet. According to insider information, the model is said to be developed under the internal code NA3 and will be based on the Neue Klasse electric architecture. First spy shots have already emerged.

title: Smart upgrades #1 with 800-volt platform
summary: While many Smart fans in Europe are eagerly awaiting the all-electric Fortwo successor, the Smart #2, the Mercedes-Benz and Geely joint venture is also updating its existing model range. The Smart #1 electric SUV is receiving a comprehensive facelift, including an 800-volt architecture and a battery capable of 6C charging.

title: Zest to install over 1,000 public EV charge points in Hertfordshire
summary: Hertfordshire County Council has selected Zest to deploy more than 1,000 public EV charge points across three districts. Backed by £1.8 million from the UK's LEVI Fund and private investment, the 15-year project targets residents without access to off-street charging.

title: Chinese SuperPanther e-truck enters series production in Austria
summary: Chinese electric truck manufacturer SuperPanther has started series production of its eTopas 600 electric tractor unit at contract manufacturer Steyr Automotive in Austria and delivered the first vehicles to customers.

title: Rock Tech secures fixed buyer for Canadian lithium
summary: Rock Tech Lithium has signed a binding offtake agreement with Geneva-based commodity trader Transamine for its Georgia Lake project in Ontario. The partnership secures the commercial marketing of the lithium mined there and includes prepayment financing of up to $80 million USD.

title: Hyundai reveals IONIQ 3 prices start at $30,000, and it already looks like a hit
summary: Hyundai says the IONIQ 3 is attracting more customer interest than any vehicle it’s ever launched. With over 300 miles of range, Hyundai’s new high-tech infotainment system, and a starting price around $30,000, the electric hatch checks all the boxes.

title: Volvo drops lidar for good on EX90 and ES90, pays owner compensation
summary: Volvo has confirmed it’s dropping lidar for good on the EX90 and ES90, and it’s paying owners compensation for a feature they were promised but will never get. In Norway, that payout is NOK 18,000 (about $1,900) per car, one of several market-by-market checks Volvo is writing after cutting ties with lidar supplier Luminar.

title: Kia’s vehicles are about to get a smart upgrade, starting in 2027
summary: Starting next year, Kia will begin launching vehicles equipped with Hyundai’s new high-tech infotainment system.

title: Vermont’s largest energy source is now a virtual power plant
summary: Green Mountain Power’s virtual power plant (VPP) – the state’s largest energy source – cut an estimated $6 million from all customers’ peak electricity costs during Vermont’s early July heat wave.

title: Tesla self-driving manager describes scary conditions in robotaxi testing
summary: A former Tesla manager who ran the company’s “Full Self-Driving” test fleet in Houston says the operation was so understaffed that its cars became “rolling hazards on public streets,” according to a lawsuit. The manager, Javier Medrano, filed the wrongful-termination complaint in Houston federal court, and its contents were reported this week. He oversaw the fleet before Tesla launched its driverless “Robotaxi” in the city.

title: You’ve heard of shared e-bikes. Now check out Veo’s new shared e-trike
summary: If you’ve spent any time in a city with shared micromobility, you’ve probably seen fleets of rental e-bikes and e-scooters waiting on street corners. But one company is betting that the next evolution of shared transportation isn’t just another bike or scooter – it’s an electric trike.

title: Mercedes’ new GLA EV leaks a day ahead of its official debut
summary: The GLA is the smallest, most affordable SUV Mercedes-Benz offers. Ahead of its debut on July 29, the first image of the all-new GLA EV leaked online.

title: Saudi Prince Alwaleed takes 5% Lucid (LCID) stake, stock jumps 25%
summary: Saudi billionaire Prince Alwaleed bin Talal has disclosed a 5% stake in Lucid Group, and the market read it as a fresh vote of Saudi confidence in the cash-strapped EV maker. Lucid (LCID) shares jumped as much as 25% on Tuesday after the filing surfaced, even though the disclosure itself is passive and mostly a technical formality.

title: Greenworks 80V CrossoverT riding mower with 600W turbo charger $1,200 off, Camplux 3.5kW to 27kW water heaters, more
summary: Our Tuesday Green Deals this week are all about home maintenance and improvements, led by the $1,200 savings on Greenworks’ 80V CrossoverT 30-inch Cordless Electric Riding Mower that comes with 4x 6.0Ah batteries and a 600W turbo wall charger at a new $2,500 low . Next, we have 3.5kW to 27kW Camplux Tankless Electric Water Heaters at some of their lowest 2026 prices starting from $108 , as well as the meross 2-Zone Wi-Fi Smart Water Timer at its $80 low . title: Baidu’s Apollo Go begins London robotaxi testing with Uber and Lyft
summary: Baidu’s Apollo Go started robotaxi road testing in London today, and it’s doing it with both of ride-hailing’s biggest names at once — Uber and Freenow by Lyft. The launch lands days after Apollo Go ran the first fully driverless trial in any right-hand-drive market, in Hong Kong. Two milestones in one week, on opposite ends of the world.

title: Volkswagen launches the cheaper ID. Polo EV after securing 25,000 orders in weeks
summary: Volkswagen opened pre-orders for the ID. Polo with the smaller 37 kWh battery, starting at under $30,000. The lower-priced model arrives after Volkswagen’s new EV received 25,000 orders weeks after it went on sale.

title: BMW ramps up iX3 output as orders near 100,000
summary: The new BMW iX3 has already received nearly 100,000 orders. Now, BMW is ramping up production at a record pace to meet the strong demand.

title: Tesla buys 90% of a 509 MW Arizona solar and storage project
summary: Tesla has signed a long-term deal to buy 90% of the output of Project Sterling, a big solar and battery plant going up in Arizona. The project pairs 509 MW of solar with a 360 MW battery, and it’s being built by ContourGlobal, the power producer owned by private equity firm KKR. It’s expected online in 2028.

title: BYD launches the ‘world’s first’ SDV kei EV, starting at just $13,000
summary: The Racco went on sale as the “world’s first SDV-based” light EV, BYD said, with a low starting price of around $13,000.

title: Mitsubishi’s ‘all-new’ Eclipse Sportback EV is a rebadged Nissan Leaf
summary: Mitsubishi is bringing a fully electric vehicle back to North America for the first time in over a decade, and it’s calling the 2027 Eclipse Sportback EV “all-new.” It isn’t. The Eclipse Sportback is a rebadged next-generation Nissan Leaf, sourced from Mitsubishi’s Alliance partner and reskinned with new bumpers and lights.

title: Yamaha is preparing to launch another electric scooter, design filings show
summary: Yamaha may not have found runaway success with its previous electric scooters , but new design filings suggest the company isn’t giving up on battery-powered two-wheelers just yet.

title: China’s EV Charging Race Just Broke The Four-Minute Barrier
summary: Hongqi says its experimental battery can add 60% charge in under four minutes with a peak charging rate of 12C.

title: We Finally Know More About The Cheap Mitsubishi Eclipse EV Coming This Fall
summary: When it finally gets here, the Eclipse EV will have dual charging ports and NACS accessibility.

title: BMW Has Already Made 50,000 iX3s. Demand Is Nearly Double
summary: The first Neue Klasse EV from BMW reached the milestone in just nine months, even as orders approach 100,000.

title: BYD's First Kei Car Takes The Fight To Toyota's Home Turf
summary: It’s the longest-range electric kei car in Japan and also the most feature packed.

title: Magnachip licenses Navitas’s GeneSiC silicon carbide technology for 1,200 V and above
summary: Magnachip Semiconductor is moving into the high-voltage and ultra-high-voltage silicon carbide market by licensing Navitas Semiconductor’s GeneSiC technology. The license covers Navitas’ Gen 4 and Gen 5 GeneSiC Trench-Assisted Planar (TAP) technologies at 1,200 V, 2,300 V, 3,300 V and higher. GeneSiC came to Navitas through its August 2022 acquisition of GeneSiC Semiconductor. Charged covered the Gen 5 platform when Navitas introduced it in February 2026. The TAP structure is the basis of Navitas’s high-voltage SiC devices for medium-voltage grid and infrastructure applications. Magnachip also gains access to Navitas’s SiC supply chain and materials ecosystem. The technology is planned to be ported, qualified and internalized at Magnachip’s fab in South Korea, and the companies expect that

title: EnerSys to dedicate its South Carolina lithium cell plant to defense applications
summary: EnerSys will dedicate the lithium cell factory it plans to build in Greenville, South Carolina, to developing and manufacturing cells for aerospace and defense applications and for specialized industrial applications that EnerSys says require a US-based supply chain. The company says the facility is intended to supply foreign entity of concern (FEOC) compliant lithium-ion cells for defense programs. EnerSys intends to transition away from its technology relationship with Verkor given the facility’s defense-focused scope, and does not expect Verkor to serve as the project’s technology partner. The company says it will instead draw on an established technology partnership within its existing aerospace and defense supply base, which it did not name. title: Ford to partner with Chinese automaker Geely to manufacture vehicles in Spain
summary: At this late hour, the “Western” automakers’ only chance of long-term survival is to partner with Chinese firms. The European brands grudgingly accepted this some time ago, and now Ford is turning down that road, announcing plans for a joint venture with Geely Auto . The JV, which will be owned two-thirds by Ford and one-third by Geely, will manufacture “low- and zero-emission vehicles” at Ford’s factory in Valencia, Spain. Ford has been losing ground in Europe for years—the Valencia factory has an annual capacity of 500,000 vehicles, but production fell below 100,000 in 2025. The new JV sounds more like a strategy to share resources and cut costs in a market in which Ford has been faltering, rather than the emergency infusion of EV technology that the company really needs. At the Spanish

title: Empower EIT commissions Dallas center, produces battery-grade lithium carbonate
summary: Empower EIT, a vertically integrated lithium technology and operating company, has begun operation of its direct lithium extraction (DLE) and conversion process at its new new 17,000-square-foot facility in Dallas. The process turns extracted lithium chloride into battery-grade lithium carbonate. The company is aiming to make its first commercial sales in 2027. Empower EIT ran five processing campaigns, each starting from eluate representing 40,000 gallons of brine, extending capabilities the company demonstrated on multiple domestic brine resources in earlier trials. The results of all five campaigns were evaluated by an independent testing lab, which verified battery-grade lithium carbonate at 99.68% to 99.91% purity. DLE pulls lithium directly from brine rather than concentrating it in

title: Megawatt charging is coming, but most test systems aren’t ready
summary: Sponsored by ITECH. As EV platforms push from 400 V to 800 V and beyond 1,000 V, engineers are facing a growing gap between charging capability and what can be safely tested in real-world conditions. This whitepaper unpacks the concept of “validation anxiety” and the risks tied to reliability, lifecycle performance, and grid interaction. It also walks through the new requirements for testing chargers, batteries, and full system integration at MW scale. Download it to understand where current test systems fall short and how to prepare for the next wave of ultra-fast charging.

title: Easelink collaborates with SEG Automotive to scale its automated EV charging system
summary: Easelink ’s Matrix Charging system enables automated conductive charging of EVs. This capability is not just about convenience—it facilitates various commercial EV applications and lays the groundwork for future autonomous mobility solutions. It also makes it easier to integrate EVs into V2G applications and other smart energy systems. Now Easelink has partnered with global automotive supplier SEG Automotive to advance the industrialization and market launch of Matrix Charging. As part of the partnership, both companies will collaborate on initial OEM series production projects. SEG Automotive is also preparing to add Matrix Charging technology to its own product portfolio. SEG Automotive will join the Matrix Charging Interest Group (MCIG), a trade group that promotes standardization of Ma

title: ZF Electrified Powertrain lead Sebastian Schmitt appointed to board
summary: Automotive supplier ZF Friedrichshafen is reshuffling its executive board. Against the backdrop of a rigorous restructuring program and persistent market challenges, Sebastian Schmitt - current head of the Electrified Drive Technologies division - is being appointed to the board. Meanwhile, CTO Peter Holdmann is departing.

title: Zurich procures 20 electric from Yutong and Daimler
summary: The Zurich City Council has approved the financial resources for the Verkehrsbetriebe VBZ to purchase 20 electric buses. The VBZ will order these from new suppliers after the existing e-buses proved to be defective.

title: Factorial and SK On to cooperate on solid-state batteries
summary: Solid-state battery developer Factorial Energy and South Korean battery giant SK On are advancing the commercialisation of solid-state cells. A newly agreed partnership will examine how existing production structures can be used for the next generation of cells.

title: Gruber Logistics electrifies component transportation for Alpitronic
summary: Charging station manufacturer Alpitronic is advancing the decarbonisation of its supply chain. For the commuter route between Auer and Bolzano in South Tyrol, transport partner Gruber Logistics is using a fully electric truck from Scania.

title: Momenta clears Level 4 test drive hurdle in Germany
summary: The German Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA) has granted Momenta, the Chinese autonomous driving specialist, nationwide approval for Level 4 test drives in urban traffic. This clears a decisive regulatory hurdle for the robotaxi project in Munich first announced a year ago.

title: BMW to cut 8,000 office jobs – primarily in Germany
summary: The automaker BMW apparently plans to cut 8,000 jobs worldwide, saving €1 billion annually. The focus is primarily on office jobs in Germany rather than production roles. The Munich-based company aims to avoid layoffs and instead offers individual severance packages.

title: MAN starts series production of MCS-ready electric trucks
summary: MAN has produced its first series-manufactured electric trucks equipped with the Megawatt Charging System (MCS) at its Munich plant. The eTGX and eTGS support charging at up to 750 kW, with the first customer deliveries now underway in nine European countries.

title: Is MCS the final word in megawatt truck charging?
summary: The Megawatt Charging System (MCS) is entering the market as the standard for high-power charging of electric trucks. But it is not the only concept under development. From six-megawatt connectors to automated underbody charging, we examine the technologies that could complement—or challenge—MCS in specific applications.

title: EU ‘Battery Booster’ funding applications now open
summary: The EU Commission has published a call for proposals to receive interest-free loans of up to €1.5 billion to support battery cell production projects.

title: Kia to build EV3 in Mexico from August
summary: Kia will also produce the EV3 in Mexico in the future. Starting August 4, the compact electric car will roll off the production line at the Pesquería plant in the state of Nuevo León. Kia also plans to sell the EV there and is therefore investing locally in charging infrastructure and renewable energies.

title: Daimler Truck recalls first-generation electric trucks
summary: Daimler Truck has launched a global recall affecting more than 131,000 commercial vehicles. Alongside diesel-powered models, the campaign also covers battery-electric trucks, specifically eActros 300 and eActros 400 vehicles equipped with AGM batteries and produced up to October 2025. The company's flagship battery-electric model, the eActros 600, is not affected.

title: Interview: Why software will define electric truck charging
summary: With dragonize's e-truck charging ecosystem, chargecloud positions itself as a technology partner for the next expansion stage of commercial vehicle electric mobility. In an interview, CEO Markus Bach explains why smart charging becomes mandatory for large e-truck fleets, the role software plays in load and energy management, and why the leap from pilot project to depot charging park is primarily a question of ensuring every truck is charged and ready when it is scheduled to leave.

title: Dongfeng presents 1.5 MW charging system
summary: Dongfeng has unveiled a prototype charging system delivering up to 1.5 MW per charging connector. The Chinese manufacturer says it will expand the portfolio with systems ranging from 720 kW to 2.4 MW for passenger cars and commercial vehicles.

title: World Premiere of the Mercedes GLA: Up to 320 kW of charging power and 657 km of range
summary: Mercedes-Benz presents the all-new GLA in Warsaw. The compact SUV has a range of up to 657 kilometers and charges at up to 320 kW. The electric car can be ordered immediately at prices starting from 48,599 euros. However, a look at the data sheets shows that the peak values only apply to two of the three models.

title: EIM joins HPCL to expand EV truck charging
summary: Energy In Motion (EIM) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) will deploy charging and battery swapping infrastructure for electric heavy-duty trucks across India. The partners plan to establish swap-and-charge hubs along key freight corridors over the next 18 to 24 months.

title: Zeekr Power opens its first megawatt-level charging station in Thailand
summary: Zeekr Power, Zeekr Group's in-house EV charging service company, has opened its first megawatt-level charging station in Thailand. It developed this site in partnership with TPM Automotive and Sinexcel.

title: BYD’s electric kei car gets off to a strong start with over 5,000 orders in its first week
summary: BYD’s electric kei car has already secured over 5,000 orders, more than half of its target by the end of 2026 in just one week.

title: China is starting to measure EV charging times in seconds, not minutes
summary: One of China’s newest EVs is also its fastest-charging, with the ability to fill its battery from 10-70% in 4 minutes and 22 seconds. But that’s not the only recent announcement of a fast-charging battery that quotes how many seconds it takes to fill up, showing that the race for fast charging has entered a new era which treats seconds as the significant figure, rather than minutes.

title: Tesla hits 10 million vehicles — but its EV growth has stalled
summary: Tesla has built its 10 millionth vehicle, the company announced this week. Ten million all-electric cars is a real milestone, and no other automaker has done it. But it’s arriving later than Tesla once promised, and the company is now building well under the capacity it already has.

title: Plug-in port: Brazilian Port of Santos electrifies DP World terminal
summary: DP World is electrifying its port fleet at the Brazilian Port of Santos with 15 battery-electric terminal trucks and three electric reach stackers in a move that marks another key step toward clean freight handling at one of Latin America’s busiest container ports.

title: IEA: Global EV sales jump 35% in Q2 and 50 countries set records
summary: Global EV sales shook off a rough start to 2026 and came bounding back in Q2, jumping 35% from the first three months of the year and setting quarterly records in 50 countries.

title: Trump feds use a solar review to approve the first AI data center on public land
summary: Apparently, a 19-megawatt (MW) solar farm and a 167-MW AI data center are “substantially the same” – at least according to the Trump administration’s Bureau of Land Management (BLM).

title: The new Mercedes GLA EV is bigger, smarter, and has a range of over 400 miles
summary: Mercedes-Benz gave its smallest SUV a glow-up. The new electric GLA offers more space for passengers, ultra-fast charging, and a range of over 400 miles.

title: The 2027 Cadillac Lyriq gains a key upgrade for $200 more
summary: The 2027 Cadillac Lyriq is now available to order. It’s only $200 more than last year’s model, but one key upgrade may make it worth the extra cost.

We’ve also got the powerful EGO Power+ 880 CFM Cordless Electric Leaf Blower with 2x 4.0Ah batteries dropping back to its $307 low . title: Ferrari’s $640K Luce EV sells out 2026 allocation: ~500 units
summary: Ferrari has already sold every Luce it plans to build in 2026. The automaker’s first electric car hit its full-year sales target — just under 500 units — in less than two months, the Financial Times reported. That’s despite a brutal wave of design criticism and a €550,000 (~$640,000) starting price that lands the EV near the top of Ferrari’s lineup.

title: Two solid-state EV battery leaders are joining forces to scale the ‘breakthrough’ tech
summary: SK On and Factorial Energy announced a new alliance that will focus on bringing solid-state batteries to the masses.

title: Waymo adds Google’s Gemini AI assistant and new UI to Ojai robotaxi
summary: Waymo is putting Google’s Gemini AI assistant inside its robotaxis for the first time, alongside the first major redesign of its rider interface in years. Both features are launching in the Ojai, Waymo’s purpose-built vehicle, as the company gets ready to open the car up to more public riders.

title: Kia opens EV3 pre-orders in Mexico ahead of US launch
summary: Kia opened pre-orders for the highly anticipated EV3 in Mexico, where the electric SUV will be built and shipped to the US later this year.

title: Huffy’s kids’ e-bike makes a compelling case for pedal-assisted riding
summary: For many parents, the idea of buying an electric bike for their kid might initially seem unnecessary. After all, didn’t we all grow up pedaling regular bikes without a motor? But the more you look at today’s generation of young riders – and the role that e-bikes can play in getting them outside – the more compelling the argument becomes. Huffy is betting on exactly that with its Quantis Kids eBike, a 24-inch electric bicycle designed for riders aged 12 and up.

title: Even China’s Truck Makers Are Building EVs In Europe Now
summary: SuperPanther and Sinotruk are now assembling electric trucks in Austria, thanks to a local contract manufacturing company.

title: Dongfeng Just Unveiled A 1.5 MW EV Charger To Take On BYD. And It’s Just Getting Started
summary: Developed in-house, Dongfeng’s flagship EV charger can cater to a wide range of battery voltages, peaking at 1,000V.

title: Genesis' First Performance Model Is Here. It Costs $71,495

title: EVgo partners with Tesla to roll out its own V4 Superchargers
summary: Tesla’s Supercharger network has often been called the gold standard of public EV charging. Now EVgo , a major public charging providers that operates some 1,200 fast charging stations in 47 states, will bring some of that Supercharger mojo to its own customers. EVgo Superchargers, owned and branded by EVgo, but operated and maintained by Tesla, will be deployed at sites “in major cities all across the US.” All will be V4 Superchargers—the latest and greatest generation, capable of charging at speeds of up to 500 kW. EVgo Superchargers will be equipped with Tesla’s Magic Dock technology, which enables CCS or NACS vehicles to charge natively without the use of an adapter. They will also offer longer charging cables, making it easier for non-Tesla EVs to conveniently plug in. Deployments are

title: Electrified Automation’s 193-120 IPM motor delivers 210 Nm for off-highway machines
summary: Electrified Automation has added the 193-120 to its 193 Series of electric motors, a low-voltage interior permanent magnet (IPM) unit built for off-highway machinery. It produces up to 210 Nm of peak torque from a 25 kg package. The 193-120 comes in 48 V and 80 V configurations. Both reach 210 Nm of peak torque and a maximum speed of 7,000 RPM, and both weigh 25 kg. Peak power is 26 kW for the 48 V version and 49 kW for the 80 V version, and rated power is 14 kW and 16.5 kW respectively. The 193-120 uses an interior permanent magnet layout that places the magnets inside the rotor, and it offers through-shaft capability. title: Pickering’s 60-191 LXI family switches currents up to 80 A
summary: Pickering Interfaces has introduced the 60-191 LXI high-current and sense switching family , which Pickering calls its highest-current switching products to date. Each unit switches signals up to 80 A and 300 V and is built to connect, disconnect and sequence multiple high-current power supplies in an automated test system. The family comes in four standard configurations, combining up to twenty 40 A and four 80 A hermetically sealed SPST-NO contactors with a complementary set of 1 A SPST relays for sense lines. Each unit occupies a 4U enclosure, and high-current and sense-line connections are made through front-panel screw terminals.
